- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract sentiment-driven pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 5–7 days to align with historical volatility decay.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.17), model underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +1–2% bias to first 5 days of forecast to account for lagged sentiment effects.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., -0.22, -0.61), model fails to anticipate reversal; add +0.5–1.5% to forecast 3–5 days after last negative sentiment peak.
